title: NY-10 candidate Brad Lander detained by IDF, group says
text:
NY-10 candidate Brad Lander detained by IDF, group says - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut POLITICS 
 Brad Lander says he was detained during West Bank olive harvest 
 Pedro Rivera has breaking details. Wednesday, October 21, 2026 11:00AM Share Follow abc7NY on Google WEST BANK (WABC) -- Brad Lander, the Democratic nominee for New York's 10th Congressional District and former New York City comptroller, said Wednesday that he was detained by the Israel Defense Forces while participating in an olive harvest in the West Bank.
 In a social media post, Lander wrote: "I've been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers. We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank." He added, "The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn't a crime under any law I know."
 According to the Israeli human rights group Rabbis for Human Rights, Lander was among roughly 90 volunteers and activists detained Wednesday while accompanying Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest near the village of Nahalin, outside Bethlehem. The group said volunteers had been helping farmers harvest olives on land they had been unable to access since Oct. 7.
 The organization said the group had been harvesting for about two hours when Israeli army, police and Border Police forces arrived and presented a military order designating the area a closed military zone for 24 hours. Representatives of the group said they agreed to comply and leave the area, but authorities nonetheless held those present for identification, photographing passports and identification cards before transporting them to a police station.
 The organization said foreign nationals were separated from Israeli volunteers.
 The detention came days after Lander announced he was traveling in the West Bank as part of the "Protect the Harvest" coalition alongside multiple advocacy groups. In a post on Monday, he said the trip's goals were to help Palestinian farmers harvest olives, document conditions in the West Bank and support efforts to protect Palestinian communities from violence and displacement. He also said the coalition sought "to secure human rights, safety, equality & freedom for both Palestinians and Israelis."
 In a statement released by Rabbis for Human Rights, Acting Executive Director Anton Goodman said, "We came to accompany farmers to land they have not been able to reach in three years, and after two hours of quiet harvesting large forces arrived and closed the area. No one could have known about this order in advance. Instead of protecting people working their own land, the army is removing them from it, and detaining those who came to stand beside them."
 It was not immediately clear whether Lander remained in custody Wednesday or whether any charges were filed.
